angle: Stop chasing model-of-the-month; build an abstraction and buy portability.
sourceTitle: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
linkedinPost:
If you’re whipsawing between AI vendors, that’s a strategy problem, not a model problem.

TechCrunch notes businesses are flipping between labs as models leapfrog—evidence that “stickiness” is thin. I see the consequences: rework, surprise bills, and brittle prompt hacks that don’t survive the next release.

The fix is an abstraction layer and a procurement shift. On the build side: a model router, eval harness with golden sets per use case, per-call SLAs (latency, quality, cost caps), and caching. Grounding data lives outside any vendor SDK.

On the buy side: portability clauses, price floors, deprecation notice periods, and usage credits that follow you across model families. Also, measure switching cost up front like a liability on the balance sheet.

Most value comes from your data, workflows, and evaluation discipline—not the logo on the box. Treat models as interchangeable components you can benchmark and swap without drama.

Question for leaders: what’s the one contract or architecture choice you’ll make now to avoid vendor lock-in later? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #AITransformation
